── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 24, 27, 37, 53 mi
This week: 40 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs a bit heavy early in the week, fine by Thursday."
Asks: "My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Last week landed exactly as planned and the marathon-pace miles hit goal pace on the nose, so this week pushes the long run back up…
Answers: (1) No, do not double up to 80 miles with doubles next week. You are at 40 miles now, were at 30 before the build, and your longest week ever was 53. (2) What actually drives a sub-3:45 is not raw mileage but a strong long run, one honest quality session, and showing up healthy on Nov 1. You are hitting all three.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off after the long run; strength or mobility if you want, no running.
Tue: easy, 6 mi, HR under 145, flat route. Loosens the legs for Wednesday.
Wed: quality, 10 mi with 7 continuous at 8:35/mi, 1.5 mi warm up and 1.5 mi cool down…
Thu: easy, 6 mi, HR under 145, conversational. Recovery from the pace work.
Fri: rest. Protect Sunday.
Sat: easy, 5 mi, HR under 145. Shakeout before the long run.
Sun: long, 20 mi, steady and easy, HR under 150, aim for 9:50 – 10:05/mi. Peak long run…
